summary.headline: Sansera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR10,213 million, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and ADS order book lifted to about INR57.5 billion.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR10,213 million, up 33% YoY, with non-auto sales of INR1,998 million up 129.9% and 20.8% of sales. EBITDA excluding exceptionals was INR1,961 million (19.2% margin, up about 200 bps YoY), after a INR126 million provision for US import duty recovery. A INR169 million exceptional litigation settlement cut reported PAT to INR874 million (8.6% margin, up 39% YoY); PAT excluding the exceptional post-tax impact was about INR1,000 million. Management raised FY27 growth commentary to high-teens, with a possible 20% plus, and said the ADS order book rose to about INR57.5 billion after a post-quarter SEM order win.

financial_highlights.value: INR169 million pre-tax; INR127 million post-tax

segments.name: ADS (aerospace, defense, semicon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,454 million, more than 3x YoY; primary non-auto growth driver. Management guides ADS growth of about 75-80% in FY27.

segments.name: Auto ICE
segments.commentary: INR6,275 million, +20.8% YoY on a high base; record quarter across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and scooters.

segments.name: Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV
segments.commentary: INR1,316 million, +22.2% YoY; record quarter, driven by EV adoption in two-wheelers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth now guided at high-teens, with management saying 20% or more is possible; non-ADS business expected to grow mid-teens to high-teens.
EBITDA margin: management wants to inch toward 19% (FY26 was 18.1%) and says Q1 may be elevated by mix, currency and about 40% international revenue; focus is on sustaining margin while growing.
ADS and export EBITDA margins targeted at 25-30%, with the upper end over time as utilisation rises.

ADS order book: about INR57.5 billion cumulative, executable over five years, versus INR44.4 billion at quarter end; the base business peak annual revenue is INR18.5 billion, to be achieved in about three years.
Management said ADS revenue will not reach INR1,500 crore next year; a FY28 revenue number will be guided toward end of FY27.

Long-term base plan: about INR3,500 crore revenue capacity by FY31 (INR5,700 crore confirmed ADS backlog executable by FY31); management reiterated INR8,000-9,000 crore total revenue opportunity by about FY31.
capex_capacity: Surface treatment facility next to ADS plant inaugurated; NADCAP validation in process, expected within about one to two months.
80,000 sq ft hangar for aero and SEM being built, commissioning expected in a month or two; customer line validation to follow.
Defense business relocating to a dedicated facility; sheet metal entry planned first via defense, later aerospace.
Build-to-suit facility of about 100,000 sq ft near the existing site under negotiation (targeted for August), ready in about 10 months.

Capacity targets: existing facility with extended hangar supports INR1,400-1,500 crore revenue; defense about INR500 crore over five years; new facility about INR1,500 crore; total about INR3,500 crore by FY31.

Auto capex: crankshaft and connecting rod forging/machining at Pantnagar (Plant 6) and Manesar (Plant 4); machining at Bangalore Plant 2 for xEV; new multi-storey building at Plant 2; projects to commission from start of Q3 FY27, completion within about a year.
ADS asset turns of 2.0-2.25x cited. Management has not updated the FY27 capex quantum given last quarter; capex phased to customer validation and utilisation.
demand_pricing: Domestic two-wheeler and passenger vehicle demand strong; management sees visibility for about one and a half quarters, with festive-season demand into Q3.
Supply chain stress on raw material and child parts; customers helping secure material.

Material cost inflation mainly in aluminium and consumables; steel inflation limited. Pass-through of steel inflation and higher tool and labour costs (mainly northern plants) still under negotiation, with nothing booked in Q1.
Forex movement gave a short-term cushion to realisations.

Exports: traction in passenger vehicles, premium two-wheelers and off-road; deliveries to a North American energy customer to give sustained revenue from Q3. Customers sourcing more from India as a stopgap while the US connecting-rod plant awaits tariff clarity.
Order wins in the quarter: about INR88 crore in PV/CV and INR75 crore in two-wheelers (normal course, per management).
Management said Sansera's motorcycle revenue grew about 12.5% and it is gaining share at TVS, Yamaha and Suzuki; it supplies about 75% of Maruti's volumes for the components it makes.

SEM order (post-quarter, after 1 July cutoff): about $75 million annual business from an existing customer; about INR5,700 crore, roughly INR1,250 crore over five years. Revenue starts calendar 2027 and peaks in calendar 2029, gated by mother-machine lead times.
